questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Boston University as my school. One for its location/city and itself is a prestigious school with a good reputation. Indeed I meet nice and professoional professors here and I am really greatful.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It's very easy. The exchange office of Boston University did a really nice job of posting all the practical information in their website and it's easy to find and informative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: visa coordination

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: not much, I don't have the choice of choosing my dream dorm. In fact, they tends to put us in big room with shared space, instead of individual room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: we can choose our meal plans but at my dorm I don't have any cooking space which is a pity

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Boston University have a lot of housing option but we don't have the power to choose, we are being decided

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The living conditions are not that good. I live in an old building with not much sun light. My dorm is depressed. I got bed bugs bitten on my legs and it's still recovering, I don't enjoy that. But it's a nice location I have to say, it's close to the campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: their email team is really helpful, they respond email very quickly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got what I want even though I was 12hrs late

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They don't allow cross-section class choosing. For example, IR studnet couldn't choose business.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I choose 3 classes. They all have heavier workloads than what I got in UCPH, and I learned a lot, even though they are BA level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say I like my host university more. American professors are more energetic and they tend to have more international conference/exchange opportunities. They are more open-minded in some ways and they are more humorous. The student-professor relationships seems to be closer in my host university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Women in the developing world; Contemporary Economic in East Asia; International Relation of Europe/EU

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Relation of Europe/EU. Professor Berger is an IR expert, he is really funny and nice. He helped me a lot and guided me to write a proper essay. You will never get bored in his class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the outing club and joined their 3 hiking activities, I enjoy it so much

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: every day have cultural events. and we can watch college athletic games at low prices. Also a lot of club offer free food, snack and merch.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: outing club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: join school event, most of them are free

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: American culture is really inclusive I like it. I embraced my identity here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: they all kind and nice

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Americans are energetic and talkative, it makes me happy

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: don't hesitate

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Boston University is really good, I enjoy every moment of it

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: professors and my new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: workload, the homework are not easy

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would like UCPH to provide more information. If you guys can let us have a little talk with the former exchangers from the same university it would be much appreciated. At least, we don't feel lonely and being up-and-down when deciding whether go or give up. I felt like you guys can do better to let us felt less lonely when we making decisions.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
